1.DialogueText: *Mary sits at her desk, slumped in her seat, anxiously watching the teacher hand back the recent test. The classroom buzzes with students talking as they glance at their grades. Mary catches a glimpse of her score: 43%. Her heart sinks.*

2.DialogueText: Mary, we’ll need to talk about this after class. That’s the fourth low score this semester. You’re capable of more.

3.DialogueText: Yeah… I know. I tried studying…?

4.DialogueText: Whoa, that bad? Don’t sweat it, though. It was a hard test.

5.DialogueText: You don’t get it. Mom’s gonna freak. I was so close this time…

6.DialogueText: Yeah, but, like, a 43? Close to what, exactly?

7.DialogueText: Okay, okay. Just... I can't go through another lecture.

8.DialogueText: Look, maybe she’ll go easy on you this time…? Anyway, are you still coming to Emma’s party tonight?

9.DialogueText: I dunno. Probably not. Mom’s already mad about my grades.

10.DialogueText: *Mary drags herself into the house, tossing her backpack by the door. Her mom is in the kitchen, prepping dinner. She looks up with a smile that quickly fades when she sees Mary’s face.*

11.DialogueText: Hey, Mary! How was school? How’d you do on that exam?

13.DialogueText: Not great? Mary, that’s the fourth bad grade this semester. What’s going on?

14.DialogueText: I dunno, Mom, it was hard! I studied for it.

15.DialogueText: Studied? Mary, if you’d been studying properly, this wouldn’t keep happening. You can’t just slide by with last-minute cramming.

16.DialogueText: Okay, fine, I get it. Can we please not do this again?

17.DialogueText: We have to, Mary! I’m not letting you go out tonight, that’s for sure. No party until your grades improve.

18.DialogueText: Are you kidding me? I really wanted to go…

19.DialogueText: Then maybe you should’ve put in more effort on that test. You’re staying in. End of discussion.

20.DialogueText: *turns away, heading to her room* Whatever…

21.DialogueText: *Mary slams her bedroom door, flopping onto her bed, staring at the ceiling. She feels trapped and frustrated, her mind buzzing with thoughts. She finally reaches for her laptop, opens it, and begins typing.*

timelinePuzzle.introText: Timeline Puzzle time! Each card shows something that happens to Mary or Sophia. Drag the cards into the empty slots so the story goes from the FIRST event to the LAST. When every slot is full, press Check. If the order is correct, you move to the next level—good luck!
timelinePuzzle.correct: Correct! Moving to the next level...
timelinePuzzle.title: Timeline Puzzle (Level {{level}})

level1.description: Put the three pictures in order so Mary stays away from a dangerous party.
level1.step1: Mary receives an online invite to a secret party from people she doesn’t know.
level1.step2: She shows the invite to her friend and asks if they should go.
level1.step3: Mary’s mom explains that parties hosted by strangers are risky, so they decide not to go.

level2.description: Arrange five steps showing how Mary blocks an online stranger.
level2.step1: A stranger messages Mary with a “modeling contract.”
level2.step2: They ask for personal details before any contract is signed.
level2.step3: Mary almost gives her address without checking who they are.
level2.step4: Her mother sees the chat and warns her to stop.
level2.step5: Mary blocks the stranger and reports it to the police.

level3.description: Put these seven steps in order to stop the fake job flyer.
level3.step1: Sophia spots a strange job flyer on the school board.
level3.step2: Sophia reads the flyer aloud and frowns.
level3.step3: Sophia shows the flyer to Mary for a second opinion.
level3.step4: Together they bring the flyer to their teacher.
level3.step5: The teacher calls the safety hotline to check it.
level3.step6: The hotline says the flyer is a scam.
level3.step7: The teacher removes the flyer and posts a warning notice.

clickPuzzle.introText: Mary needs your help to escape a dangerous situation. Guide her through three locations by finding tools and solving puzzles.
clickPuzzle.howToPlay: Click objects to interact. Collect items and use them together from your inventory.
clickPuzzle.objective: Help Mary escape by finding tools and solving each level's puzzle!
clickPuzzle.tapStart: (Click outside to start the escape mission)

emojiDecoder.introText: Traffickers and groomers rarely say what they want. They hide it in compliments, gifts, slang and emojis. You'll review real-style message threads Mary and her friends received, and work out what's really going on.
emojiDecoder.introStep1Text: Check the profile clues too: account age, mutual friends, what doesn't add up.
emojiDecoder.introStep2Text: Tap every message that's a manipulation tactic. Not every message is one, and false alarms cost points.
emojiDecoder.introStep3Text: Work out what an emoji combo really means in this conversation.
emojiDecoder.introStep4Text: Pick the safest response. Some answers are only partly right.
emojiDecoder.introNote: {{count}} cases. Points for every red flag you catch, every code you crack, and every safe move.
emojiDecoder.flagText: Tap each message that uses a manipulation tactic. Tap again to remove a flag.
emojiDecoder.flagHint: Not every message is dangerous. Flagging innocent messages costs a point each.
emojiDecoder.revealNoFlags: This thread had no red flags
emojiDecoder.falseAlarms_one: {{count}} false alarm: an innocent message you flagged.
emojiDecoder.falseAlarms_other: {{count}} false alarms: innocent messages you flagged.
emojiDecoder.rank_expert_text: You read between the lines like a pro. You spotted the tactics, cracked the codes, and made safe calls.
emojiDecoder.rank_sharp_text: You caught most of what was going on. Look at the tactics you missed: they're the ones that work best on people.
emojiDecoder.rank_training_text: These tactics are designed to feel normal. That's why they work. Go through the tactic file below and try again.
emojiDecoder.safetyTitle: If this ever happens to you
emojiDecoder.safety1: Don't reply, pay or send anything
emojiDecoder.safety4: Tell a trusted adult. It's never your fault
emojiDecoder.helpline: In the Netherlands you can talk to De Kindertelefoon for free and anonymously on 0800‑0432, or get help with online abuse at helpwanted.nl.

wordChoice.introText: Groomers and traffickers hide risk in ordinary-sounding words. You'll read short scenes Mary gets online, then pick the word that names what's really going on — or the safest move.
wordChoice.introStep1Text: A short context line sets up who is talking and why it matters.
wordChoice.introStep2Text: Choose the word that fits. Wrong options are meant to sound almost right.
wordChoice.introStep3Text: Every answer comes with a short debrief so the pattern sticks.
wordChoice.introNote: {{count}} questions. {{points}} points for each correct word.
wordChoice.previewContext: A new DM. Mary doesn’t know this person.
wordChoice.previewBefore: “Hang out tonight, no parents.” Traffickers use
wordChoice.previewAfter: to keep teens away from safe adults.
wordChoice.tip1: Ask: does this cut Mary off from adults or friends?
wordChoice.tip2: Urgency, secrecy, and “prove it” are common pressure tools.
wordChoice.tip3: If two words feel close, pick the one that names the risk.
wordChoice.rank_expert_text: You named {{correct}} of {{total}} correctly. You can tell when “nice” language is actually a trap.
wordChoice.rank_sharp_text: You got {{correct}} of {{total}}. Review the tactics you missed — those are the ones that sound the most normal.
wordChoice.rank_training_text: {{correct}} of {{total}} this round. These words are designed to feel ordinary. That’s why the practice matters.
wordChoice.safetyTitle: If this ever happens to you
wordChoice.safety1: Don’t reply, pay, or send anything
wordChoice.safety4: Tell a trusted adult. It’s never your fault
wordChoice.helpline: In the Netherlands you can talk to De Kindertelefoon for free and anonymously on 0800‑0432, or get help with online abuse at helpwanted.nl.
